what: Letters are stacked in two vertical sets, and on hover they roll up one line so the second set rises — with a per-letter delay (default .03s) one letter at a time, with 0 the whole word rolls. A faint first set → bold second set swap is also possible. Current page link (aria-current=page) stops where it rolled

options.stagger: Delay between characters (sec), default .03 — 0 means whole word
options.tone: With ”dim” the first set is --kf-dim and the second set is --kf-ink · with ”ink” the first set keeps the inherited color and only the second set is --kf-ink (beige text turning white, Brand A) · with ”under” the first set keeps the inherited color and only the second set rising from below is --kf-dim (the gray shadow copy of Brand B)
options.mode: With ‹once›, each time the pointer comes over it the whole word rolls once (ignoring delay) and the second layer rises, then returns to its place. It does not roll back when the pointer leaves, and it rolls again only after another hover (Brand A: dur .75 · ease 0.19,1,0.22,1 · gap 2). With ‹hold›, the enter plays through for hold seconds before the leave is accepted, and the leave returns to place at once with no curve. If the pointer returns in between, it carries on from there (Brand B: stagger .02 · dur 1.2 · ease 0,0.8,0.17,1 · hold .8).
options.gap: Gap between the two sets — a number is px, with a unit it is used as is (.4167vw), default 0. The second set sits below 100% + gap and rolls that much further (Site A mode: once 2 · Site B default form .4167vw) · in mode: hold too the first set rises to −(100% + gap) (Site C 20% — original first set −120% · clone 110%)
options.hold: Length in seconds that mode: hold keeps the entrance held, default .8 — original data-enter-time
options.back: If “end”, on leaving it reverses from the last letter (default is from the first letter, as on entering)
options.cut: In mode: once, cuts the roll at this many seconds and snaps back in place — if it comes back into view before the cut, it does not roll again. Default none (rolls to the end) (city site: dur 1 · ease 0.19,1,0.22,1 · cut .6)
options.skew: Roll the whole line at an angle (deg) — the line rolls as one piece, not letter by letter, the first copy leaves tilting by skewY around the bottom right, and the second comes up already tilted and straightens around the bottom left (century: skew: 32; stagger: 0; dur: .6; ease: 0.25,0.1,0.25,1 — CSS ease)
options.frames: mode: once — number of frames to wait before rolling, default 2 (two frames after the clone is attached) — 0 rolls as soon as the pointer touches, and re-entering while it is rolling does not start a new roll (original site)
options.lead: In mode: once, only the first set moves up and fades out over this many seconds (the second set rises in over dur) — no default (both sets roll together). Brand: lead .6 · lead-ease 0.25,0.46,0.45,0.94 · dur .4
options.lead-ease: lead’s curve is of the type ‹0.87,0,0.13,1›, same as the default ease
options.drip: If ‹down›, the whole line drops. On hover the first set stretches vertically up to 2.4x (blur 3.5px · three blood-stain shadows smearing upward) and falls out downward, while the same letters drop in from above and settle. The stretch is a .85s linear keyframe, the move is a .6s linear() curve that briefly pulls up and then slams down, and on leave it is .35s cubic-bezier(.2,1,.3,1) · If ‹up›, it runs in reverse, upward (Brand menu down · footer to-top up). dur · ease · out are accepted as they are.
options.by: With ‹word› the stagger is applied per word instead of per character — spaces are left as they are (Brand button · header link: .02s word interval · .2s · 0.65,0,0.35,1)
options.look: With ‹serif›, only the second copy switches to the title font (--kf-font-display) and aligns to the center of the first copy — the sans-serif letters slide up and out while the same letters rise in as serif (reference menu · back to top: stagger: 0.015; dur: 0.8; ease: 0.215,0.61,0.355,1; gap: 0.1em; look: serif)
options.dir: With ”down” the second copy hides on top of the first and drops down one line to sit in place — the same letters seem to fall from above and swap (Brand menu · View More: stagger: 0; dur: .4; ease: 0.43,0.05,0.17,1; dir: down)
options.outease: Leaving curve in the form ”0.215,0.61,0.355,1” — if omitted, same as ease
options.space: If “skip”, spaces don’t take up a delay slot (only letters are sequenced)
options.lag: The extra wait (seconds) before the first letter starts in mode: hold, default 0 — for when the original starts one cell late with (i+1)× delay (brand .05)
